description: A Steiner Parker filter with three ways in, one for each of lowpass, bandpass and highpass, mixed into a single output

params.text: Sets the cutoff frequency, 16Hz to 16384Hz as a power of two
Attenuates the voltage at the Freq jack before it is added to the Freq knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Sets the resonance, 0 to 2; the higher it is the less the filter is damped and the harder it rings at the cutoff
Attenuates the voltage at the R jack before it is added to the R knob, 0 to 1

inputs.text: The signal to be filtered lowpass, one per channel
The signal to be filtered bandpass, one per channel
The signal to be filtered highpass, one per channel
Modulates the resonance, a fifth per volt scaled by the R CV knob
Modulates the cutoff, one octave per volt scaled by the Freq CV knob

outputs.text: The three filtered signals added together

notes: the three inputs are the three ways into one filter rather than three separate filters, so patching the same signal into two of them mixes those responses
the cutoff is held between 2Hz and a third of the sample rate however far the knob and the jack push it
the channel count of the output is that of whichever of the three inputs carries the most channels

inputs.3:
continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1.999V.
inputs.4:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the Freq knob alone; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
